HRA Analysis: SKIP TO ME LOU (5) was forced to race without cover last time out and just couldn’t quite reel in Atula. He looks set to get a similar run in this race but is likely to have derived good benefit from the first up outing. BLACKJACK SAM (1) has a good draw in this race and good enough gate speed to drive through and lead before having options from there. He got back in the run last time out and was running on nicely late. BLACKJACK (4) comes into this race first up from NZ and boasts just a moderate career record. Ran well in his latest outing finishing second running on strongly late in a race the winner dashed up a quick enough last quarter of 27.9. JUSTANOTHER TORQUE (2) looks likely to get a soft run behind the speed in this race. She put in a very good run three starts ago sitting without cover at Redcliffe and running second. SELECTIONS: SKIP TO ME LOU (5), BLACKJACK SAM (1), BLACKJACK (4), JUSTANOTHER TORQUE (2) SUGGESTED BET: SKIP TO ME LOU (5) to win.

TRACER BULLET (6) was able to secure a good run two starts ago over the 2040 at Redcliffe and ran over the top late to score. He should get a similar run in this race and can be hard to hold out late. SKYLAR BREE (3) wasn’t beaten far last time out in what may have been a stronger race taken out by Deep Regret over Rosie Pollen. She has worked back into some better form in recent outings and hadn’t had a lot of luck in her starts prior. MADAM WEST (1) should secure a good run on the pegs just behind the speed in this race. She didn’t have a lot of luck at Redcliffe last time out when drawing awkwardly and being shuffled a long way back. DOOLITTLE DOOZZIE (5) was able to score nicely last time out when sweeping over the top late to win. She has always seemingly liked racing over the middle trip and could be running on late again. SELECTIONS: TRACER BULLET (6), SKYLAR BREE (3), MADAM WEST (1), DOOLITTLE DOOZZIE (5) SUGGESTED BET: TRACER BULLET (6) to win.

NONIS GOLD CLASS (10) was able to win a much stronger race last time out when leading and taking them all the way. She is not as well handicapped this time but does look the class horse and just needs to bring her best manners to be hard to beat. BUSTER DAN (11) was able to score nicely last time out beating Black Viper after securing a good run close to the speed. He finds a very similar race and is set to be hard to beat again in this race. VICTREE VIC (5) returns from a spell in this race for new trainer Shawn Grimsey. He was fancied last time out to take out what might’ve been a harder race from the mobile at this track and with better manners in this race could be hard to beat. ITS ALL RIGHT NOW (7) was able to run well last time out in a similar type of race taken out by BUSTER DAN (11). She was forced to race without cover there and could secure a more economical run in this race. SELECTIONS: NONIS GOLD CLASS (10), BUSTER DAN (11), VICTREE VIC (5), ITS ALL RIGHT NOW (7) SUGGESTED BET: NONIS GOLD CLASS (10) to win.

ONE CHAIN ROAD (1) has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead this race in the early stages. He led two starts ago and was run down late by VICTREE CHARLIE (6) who was able to settle much closer than usual in that race. DIGBY DEVIL (9) looks suited in this race from a draw where he will do no work early. He raced without luck last time out when drawing wide and being shuffled back before making a wide run into it. DEEP REGRET (4) sat without cover and proved too good for Rosie Pollen at this track last time out. He finds a tougher race but is going well and can’t be ruled out. BETTYS GOLD CLASS (8) should get the perfect run through early in this race behind a gate speed horse. She was close up last time out over the less suitable 2138 behind Smirks Lika Boss. SELECTIONS: ONE CHAIN ROAD (1), DIGBY DEVIL (9), DEEP REGRET (4), BETTYS GOLD CLASS (8) SUGGESTED BET: ONE CHAIN ROAD (1) to win.

RUBY RHAYNE BOW (5) was able to work to the lead last time out at this track and took them all the way beating Sweet Rocky. She should be able to work forward in this race and find a prominent position and should be hard to beat from there. LILSTREPO (2) was excellent four starts ago sitting without cover and just being run down late by Dougs Flame. She should get a good run in this race and should be hard to beat. APOLLO DREAMZ (8) should get a good run through early in this race. He was a much better run last time out when running into third late behind Charge Ahead at this track over the 2138. MISS BAY KING COLE (1) was able to lead and win three starts ago at this track to make it two in a row there having won after racing leaders back her start prior. She has a good draw in this race and should be close enough in the run. SELECTIONS: RUBY RHAYNE BOW (5), LILSTREPO (2), APOLLO DREAMZ (8), MISS BAY KING COLE (1) SUGGESTED BET: RUBY RHAYNE BOW (5) to win.

IDEAL PURSUIT (6) has a reasonable draw on the front row and can look to press forward and lead in this race. The distance of the race does appear a query for her but she has previously run well at this track and trip. BRACKEN WARRIOR (1) has good gate speed and should be able to lead easily before having options from there. He led three starts ago and was very good just being run down late by Miss Bay King Cole in fast time. He should go well from an ideal draw. MIGHTY IDEAL (8) has a good draw in this race and will just need luck at the right time. He was well driven last time out to weave into the clear and run over the top late. ULTIMATE ARK (9) got back in the run last time out at Redcliffe and was making up late ground into sixth behind Terragong Swinger. He looks suited over the distance and should get a good run through in the early stages of the race. SELECTIONS: IDEAL PURSUIT (6), BRACKEN WARRIOR (1), MIGHTY IDEAL (8), ULTIMATE ARK (9) SUGGESTED BET: ULTIMATE ARK (9) to win.

SOHO CASABLANCA (1) has been building back towards his best form since returning from a spell and coming into this race fourth up he could be nearing peak fitness. He got back in the run last time out and was making up some ground late behind Sweet Dior. He could lead and be hard to run down. BENNYDASOOK (7) returns from a spell in this race and draws widest on the front row. He was very impressive last time in winning four of his last six starts and was able to rate fast time at this track. If he’s ready to go first up he should be hard to beat. ALL EYES ON BLING (8) should get a good run through behind the potential leader in the early stages of this race. She ran a good race last time out finishing fourth behind Ruby Rhayne Bow at this track. LETHAL LOUIE (3) was checked at a crucial stage last time out when making his run into it at Redcliffe. He may get shuffled back in this race and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: SOHO CASABLANCA (1), BENNYDASOOK (7), ALL EYES ON BLING (8), LETHAL LOUIE (3) SUGGESTED BET: ALL EYES ON BLING (8) each way. SMARTER THAN YOU (1) has been in excellent form this campaign and draws ideally in this race. He has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead in the early stages which should see him very hard to run down. DOUGS FLAME (8) was very well driven last time out to nab the leaders back trail and did well there to hang on for third behind the very smart pair of Final Deadline and Fate Awaits. She should get a good run through early in this race and should be suited by the step back to 1660. BAINBRIDGE (2) starts first up in this race for the stable of Trent Dawson having previously done his racing in NSW. He is a horse with very high speed and should be suited by the soft draw in this race where he can settle close to the speed without doing too much work. MOSSDALE TERRY (9) should secure a good run off the speed in this race and has been racing well. He ran well three starts ago finishing second behind Isla Rochelle over the 2138 at this track. SELECTIONS: SMARTER THAN YOU (1), DOUGS FLAME (8), BAINBRIDGE (2), MOSSDALE TERRY (9) SUGGESTED BET: SMARTER THAN YOU (1) to win.

FIFTY THREE STARS (2) should have the gate speed to work forward and find the lead in the early stages of this race from a good draw. He drew poorly last time out and was making up good ground late to not be beaten too far by Our Rocky in a strong race. He looks hard to beat. QUIK CHANGE (1) draws ideally in this race and can lead before having options from there. In this type of grade he seems to be best when driven with a sit which should see him get every chance in this race. SPUNKYS GOTSECRETS (7) was forced to race without cover last time out over the 1660 and battled on well there to finish second behind smart Kiwi Mostart. He may be left to do the work again in this race from a wide draw but should run well again. STARZZZ DESTINY (4) was able to show good gate speed last time out to lead and run well from there for third. He should be able to press forward and race in a prominent position from a reasonable draw and should be thereabouts again. SELECTIONS: FIFTY THREE STARS (2), QUIK CHANGE (1), SPUNKYS GOTSECRETS (7), STARZZZ DESTINY (4) SUGGESTED BET: FIFTY THREE STARS (2) to win.

MOSTERT (2) didn’t have much luck on QLD debut when making a wide run into it before just being nabbed late by Beyond Doubt. He was able to then break through nicely last time out making a wide run into it to score a good win. If he can work to the lead this time he is likely to take plenty of running down. TARGARYEN (1) should be able to secure a good run behind the speed in this race from the ideal draw. He was left without cover which doesn’t usually suit him and was able to battle on nicely for third. He should be hard to hold out late. HES ALL TORQUE (8) should get a good run through behind a horse which is likely to settle close in the run. He was able to score a hat-trick of wins recently which included a win in the showcase final at Redcliffe after starting from a 40m handicap and breaking the track record. STORMTIDE (3) has really bounced back into impressive form recently scoring a good win earlier in the week when running over the top to beat Rock Hammer. He should settle close enough and looks a horse which could add value to exotics in this race. SELECTIONS: MOSTERT (2), TARGARYEN (1), HES ALL TORQUE (8), STORMTIDE (3) SUGGESTED BET: MOSTERT (2) to win.

LEAP TO FAME (7) returned in terrific style last time out when being forced to race outside of Captain Shuffles who attempted to run him off his legs first up from a spell over the 1660. It looked as though for a brief moment Captain Shuffles may have had the upper hand before Leap To Fame kicked into another gear and just cruised on by running through the line powerfully and winning with authority rating a brilliant 1.49.1 mile rate. This looks an easier assignment in this race and it appears the only question is times and margins. TIMS A TROOPER (5) was able to show enough speed to drive through and lead last time out in a race where they went a frantic tempo setting it up for DASHING (6) to run over the top late. He is likely to be driven a touch more conservatively early this time and can look to be running on late. DASHING (6) was able to return nicely from a spell last time out when getting back and being suited by a frantic tempo which allowed him to run over the top late and beat Manila Playboy. He is a horse with relatively good gate speed and from a wide draw has options in the early stages of this race. DISTRICT ATTORNEY (4) secured a good run last time out behind Captain Shuffles when battling on reasonably for fourth. If he could zip across early in this race he would have rough top three claims and reasonable top four claims. SELECTIONS: LEAP TO FAME (7), TIMS A TROOPER (5), DASHING (6), DISTRICT ATTORNEY (4) SUGGESTED BET: TIMS A TROOPER (5) to win.

NEXT TO ME (1) should have the gate speed to drive through and lead this from the ideal draw. He secured a good run last time out in a very strong race taken out by Our Rocky and wasn’t beaten too far there. He should run well. JOHN WAYNE (4) drew poorly last time out when running a good fourth at this track. He was very good winning recently over the 2040 at Redcliffe. He should be suited by the distance of this race and looks to have good each way claims. BETTOR CHEER (9) was forced to make a very wide run into it last start and was making up good ground into second. He should get a good run off the speed and can be running on late again. ROCK HAMMER (3) led last time out and may have just gone a bit too fast out in front when being run down by Stormtide after rolling along throughout. He should settle close from a low front row draw and has claims with the right run. SELECTIONS: NEXT TO ME (1), JOHN WAYNE (4), BETTOR CHEER (9), ROCK HAMMER (3) SUGGESTED BET: NEXT TO ME (1) to win.

SALLY BIGTIME (7) drew poorly last time out and was left without cover there battling on well for third behind Golden Fire and Tremendous Sensation. She draws poorly again this time but finds a much weaker race and should be able to settle close enough and run well from there. LUVARECHS (1) has moderate gate speed and should be able to drive through and hold a prominent position early. She has been unlucky to bump into Golden Fire on a number of occasions this campaign and could be suited finding a race without her this time. ISLA ROCHELLE (2) has a great draw in this race to settle close enough without doing too much work in the early stages. She was an impressive winner rating good time at this track three starts ago running over the top late. DEBBIE LINCOLN (3) returns from a spell in this race having trialled up nicely winning a recent trial. She has high speed and should go well from a low draw where she can settle close in this race. SELECTIONS: SALLY BIGTIME (7), LUVARECHS (1), ISLA ROCHELLE (2), DEBBIE LINCOLN (3) SUGGESTED BET: SALLY BIGTIME (7) to win.

GOLDEN SUNSET (1) should be able to drive through and lead in this race. She was excellent last time out when running over the top to score a nice win. She should run well again in this race. KEAYANG STUKA (5) has recently changed stables and starts first up in this race. He ran fourth two starts ago in the first round of heats of the Inter Dominion after starting one of the favourites in a race taken out by Lovemeto. He looks well placed in this race. PINNIE (2) looks likely to get a very economical run in this race just behind the speed. She sat close to the speed last time out in a race taken out by key rival GOLDEN SUNSET (1) last time out from the stand start. LOVE GUN (3) should get a good run just off the speed in this race. He was forced to race without cover last time out and could be better suited with a softer run. SELECTIONS: GOLDEN SUNSET (1), KEAYANG STUKA (5), PINNIE (2), LOVE GUN (3) SUGGESTED BET: GOLDEN SUNSET (1) to win.

FEAR THE PAIN (1) has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead in the early stages of this race. She was left without cover last time out and wasn’t suited by that run in a race taken out by Golden Shooz which was dominated by runners on the pegs. THE LADY DIOR (4) was able to work to the lead two starts ago and rated good time there when finishing second behind Harperville. She should settle close enough in this race from the front row draw and looks to find a suitable race. SO MANY MOMENTS (8) should get a good run through in this race behind a gate speed horse. She ran a good second two starts ago behind Miss Bay King Cole and with a similar effort she should run well again. PRINCESS OF SAVOY (3) was seemingly a touch disappointing on QLD debut finishing sixth after securing a soft run on the pegs. She is likely to have derived benefit from the outing and can run a better race second up. SELECTIONS: FEAR THE PAIN (1), THE LADY DIOR (4), SO MANY MOMENTS (8), PRINCESS OF SAVOY (3) SUGGESTED BET: FEAR THE PAIN (1) to win. OVERVIEW:MISS ADDI (4) brings one of the strongest profiles of the program, with a strong record at this track and distance range, and comes off some first-rate form, including a win here two back when able to lead, with strong placings around that, including at Melton. There’s speed inside here, but the smaller field should allow her to map favourably and produce solid final sectionals, which she’s consistently been doing this time in. MASTER LOUEY (1) looks the main danger from the soft pole draw, with Herbertson aboard and the likelihood he will get his chance along the sprint lane after doing little work, trailing the speed as he’s done recently at this track. It all depends on the tempo and the momentum he gets into the straight as to whether he can run down the top pick. HILTONS SPIRIT (2) deserves respect based on current form, which has seen him win 3 from 10 this season, along with some solid recent sectionals last start at Melton. This is another strong race, but his soft map has him in the mix. KEAYANG SANTIAGO (3) is an interesting runner returning to VIC and his former stable, and did perform well earlier in the year. He has early gate speed and will no doubt look to be on the front end; just prefer to see him against this line-up. WOTDIDUSAAY (6) caused a big upset at Echuca and deserves consideration on that effort; this draw makes things a little tricky, however. BACK: MISS ADDI (4) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:MISS ADDI (4), MASTER LOUEY (1), HILTONS SPIRIT (2), KEAYANG SANTIAGO (3)

OVERVIEW:CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7) has been very honest, being runner-up in 4 of 6 attempts and racing well at this track. He got a good run and bumped into a handy one last time and just couldn’t match those sectionals when 2nd, while his runs prior were good, often from tricky draws. No favours with his marble again, but I fancy this is one of his most winnable opportunities. TOMBEUR (5) creates interest as a first starter off a trial win in slow time recently, and that was his first outing in a year. He’s from one of the state’s best stables, so monitor any strong market support. MEGALODON (8) is a well-named son of the mare Classic Shark and has shown promise in two career outings, finishing 3rd on both occasions. He goes from better draws to the back row but can get an economical peg run here and get his chance late. SIR KITT (1) is a 2yo who struck a very strong bunch of his own age on debut and now takes on more experienced types. He has a soft draw, and these shouldn’t put down the sectionals he faced last time, so he is open to improvement. BACK: CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7), TOMBEUR (5), MEGALODON (8), SIR KITT (1)

OVERVIEW:LIBERTY STAR DUST (5) is racing well, with a good win four back at Kilmore when given an ace drive, then went very close to winning at Geelong two back. Around those efforts, he was racing against the elite of his age group in the Vicbred Series. He’s only had the one start at Cranbourne for a win, and although he’ll need luck from the draw, he is a strong winning hope. CYCLONE JENNI (7) did a really nice job in winning from an awkward draw at this track four back and has been a little out of her depth class-wise since in the Vicbred. The draw is very tricky here but she deserves respect based on what she’s capable of. STORM VENDETTA (1) looks to get a very cosy run from the inside draw and has been racing well in his three runs for the new stable. He meets a few handy ones but must be included in exotics. HEZ HARRYWHO (2) finds a good draw and distance here to buck the trend of form he’s been in. That was the case four back when he found the front over the mile and wasn’t for catching at Kilmore. Look for a big bounce back on those key form indicators. FARROH JOE (3) is a 2yo taking on the older horses here and has run well in similar circumstances before, albeit in slightly easier company. He placed 2nd in his heat and 7th in the final of the Vicbred Series. WEONA OUR RIGHTS (4) is going okay, with his only failure to place this season coming when he drew wide in a Vicbred heat. He’s in the mix with the right run. SELECTIONS:LIBERTY STAR DUST (5), CYCLONE JENNI (7), STORM VENDETTA (1), HEZ HARRYWHO (2)

OVERVIEW: A good-quality race with a mix of 2 and 3yos, with the younger pair of LETITRIDELUV (2) and filly TWIGSTAR (3) looking the standout options. It’s agonising to make a definitive call between two horses who are racing so well at this level, but I must lean to TWIGSTAR (3) based on her excellent debut where she settled back in the field and ran away from them over the short trip. She now has a more favourable draw to press forward over the longer trip and potentially look for the lead. She’s already proven she can run time and, with natural improvement, will be very hard to catch. LETITRIDELUV (2) already has a decent scalp in his career in winning his maiden, then has acquitted himself very well against the elite of his age group in the Vicbred Series. He didn’t draw well in any of those races, and this favourable marble guarantees a positive map and every chance to win again; it’s just whether he’s capable of running times comparable to what the top pick did on debut. Would be surprised if that isn’t the quinella, with much of the remainder having claims at the minor end. BROADWAY OBSESSION (9) may be next best based on a strong SP profile and a solid place strike rate, with SWEET LADY LOU (8) and CALIFORNIA COOL (1) both benefiting from being on the peg line in what should be a strong last half. BACK: TWIGSTAR (3) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:TWIGSTAR (3), LETITRIDELUV (2), BROADWAY OBSESSION (9), SWEET LADY LOU (8)

OVERVIEW: Tricky race, being a standing start over the long distance for trotters and not presenting with the most reliable form under the conditions. EMWALLEN (3) has the most upside, being a lightly raced 5yo, winning 4 from 12 including two solid wins when able to lead all the way recently. This is his first crack under standing-start conditions, which is a slight concern considering some of his rivals love the tapes, but if you’re willing to take the risk, his ability can carry him a long way. MAESTRO (8) ticks a few boxes, being the most reliable and adept under standing-start conditions, a country cup winner under similar conditions and securing the services of Chris Alford. He’s a horse who seems to keep coming under slogging conditions, so he can overcome the back mark here. AVANT GUARD (7) will appreciate facing this sort of quality, having raced better types his past few. He was a winner in similar class four back but under mobile conditions. He’s yet to win from the tapes, but this is his best chance. EL CONQUEROR (5) likes the stand and longer trips and brings a favourable SP profile considering the opposition here. He doesn’t win out of turn, but his manners and the opportunity to get in front of some key rivals hold him in good stead. There’s a host of others worth considering, such as SOVEREIGN TIGER (6), who likes this track and is a last-start winner in easier company, and NEPHEW OF SONOKO (9), who, although he prefers mobile conditions, strikes the easiest race he’s faced in a while. SELECTIONS: EMWALLEN (3), MAESTRO (8), AVANT GUARD (7), EL CONQUEROR (5)

OVERVIEW: JUSTLIKEDAVE (7) was able to lead from this draw two back over the shorter trip and bolted in, winning by 18m and running fast time. He ran 2nd last start when a very short-priced favourite, but the run was still good after over-racing back in the field. His record over anything longer than the sprint journey is a concern, but his best form is hard to ignore. ROBLEN RANGER (2) could be a good roughie here, 2nd up from a break after doing plenty of work fresh. He has good speed to utilise this inside draw and map well. He can give cheek at a price and goes in the Quaddie for sure, no matter the odds. ROBLEN DEMON (5) is his stablemate and has been in good form this preparation, sitting tough and winning here two back. The map may be a little tricky but he can strike with the right run. The back-row runners BONA KHAN (8) and ALTA BAYAMO (9) can be very hard to catch, particularly from back-row draws, but they are worth keeping safe with the extra distance should those at the top end overcook things. BACK: ROBLEN RANGER (2) – 0.5 units (win) 1.5 units (place) SELECTIONS: JUSTLIKEDAVE (7), ROBLEN RANGER (2), ROBLEN DEMON (5), BONA KHAN (8)

OVERVIEW:SIR CANDY CLOUD (1) has the advantage of the concession to use a coveted pole draw and his good gate speed to get a comfortable lead over the short trip. He’s run well in his two runs with recent G1-winning driver Blake Pace aboard, and if he can tap the brakes in the middle section and get a lungful of air for the finish, he will be hard to run down. REASON TO LOVE (8) can catch his cover on the peg line and didn’t have much luck last time from a similar position. He can be an improver from the map and should be included in all multiples. CHASING THE WIND (9) has been popular with punters the past couple with Alford aboard, and having to do no work and come with one run here may suit depending on the tempo. ROCKNROLL RAMBO (10) is threatening to win, placing at his last four starts, but he goes to the back-row draw over the short trip, which hurts his chances. However, the closing sectionals shouldn’t be overly quick for him to make up ground late. DELTA STARZ (5) had a flat tyre last time and can improve based on his win four back, while it’s hard to know what to make of POWERLINC (6), but he is worth throwing in the wider Quaddie should you want to be safe. BACK: SIR CANDY CLOUD (1) – 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: SIR CANDY CLOUD (1), REASON TO LOVE (8), CHASING THE WIND (9), ROCKNROLL RAMBO (10)

OVERVIEW: PICKLE IT (5) looks the starting point here in a very even race where map and conditions will play a major part. This horse is a very quick beginner, relishes the mile and has a strong record at the track of 29:4-4-8. He’s probably been run off his legs with the times put down his past few, but those times are unlikely here, so he can hold on with the right tempo. OHHEMJAY CRESCO (1) is a one-batter who will be doing his best to hunt up from the pole, but he proved last start at Wagga that when he can roll along, he’s hard to get past. There are several horses that are map-dependent but are going well enough to include: GOZO MAJOR (4), DOT BALL (6), QUICK CRUNCH (7), FINAL BOW (8) and TOPHUT JOHNY (9). If things worked out, a win by any of them wouldn’t surprise at all. Maybe throw them all in the Quaddie if you want to go wide. SELECTIONS:PICKLE IT (5), OHHEMJAY CRESCO (1), QUICK CRUNCH (7), TOPHUT JOHNY (9)

There looks to be some nice gate speed from the well-drawn runners across the front row over the mile here. JUST LIKA DREAM (4) continues to run good races without winning. She found the front and was run down by her stablemate last start, although in quick time, and would expect her to again push forward from the middle front-row draw to find a spot on speed. DOLCE DRAMA (3) is another that has been racing well without winning and should find a nice position on speed with cover, giving her every chance. OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (2) is first up in the state and looks well placed and drawn to figure prominently in the finish, especially dropping back in grade. She looks likely to be first to the pegs if OUR FATAL CHARM (1) is happy to take a sit, as she has at her past few starts. EYE SEE AMOUR (8) could be dangerous late if the gaps come her way from the pegs draw, while GOBSMACKED (11) will be hoping for some genuine speed to allow him to run home strongly from his usual outside back-row draw. KNOCK OUT (6) improved last start when narrowly beaten but finds an awkward draw here, as does BUSLOAD OF FAITH (7), who was able to find the front and hold off the challengers when breaking through last start. Selections:OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (2), DOLCE DRAMA (3), JUST LIKA DREAM (4), GOBSMACKED (11) Staking Strategy:OUR ULTIMATE GRACY draws inside the main dangers and gets her chance to break through first up in the state. 2 unit win – OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (2).

A No More Than Two Wins event for the three-year-olds, where SUMTHIN ELSE (6) is first up in the state for the new stable after being competitive in the Vicbred three-year-old series of late. You would expect that form to hold up well in this type of event and see her right in the finish. IYLAC CHAMBER (7) was terrific at his past two starts before going for a let-up, doing plenty of work in the run and still managing to hold his rivals off. He should continue to improve this preparation after two nice trials ahead of his return here. A ROCKN NIGHTMARE (3) ran well first up in the state and gets a nice draw to find a prominent position with cover, which should give er every chance. The back-row runners QUALIFY (8) and HIGH BELIEVER (9) have consistently been earning cheques in these grades and should be running home into the money with a nice run in transit. BRIGHTLY BLAZE (5) could be the knockout hope if she can find a nice position in the field with some genuine tempo throughout. Selections:IYLAC CHAMBER (7), SUMTHIN ELSE (6), HIGH BELIEVER (9),A ROCKN NIGHTMARE (3) Staking Strategy: In what looks a very even affair, A ROCKN NIGHTMARE has a good draw to find a nice spot on speed. 2 unit win – A ROCKN NIGHTMARE (3).

The low-class race here tonight is, as usual, hard to assess, with not a whole lot of great exposed form to go off. KIAVINO STRIDE (8) is the 285-start veteran and should benefit from the small field, allowing him to put himself into the race at some point and look to hold them off late, which may be enough to win here. KUHIO KREST (6) has been somewhat disappointing of late after a nice first-up effort in the state, but expect he may be driven with a sit here and look to run home strongly. SWEET AMOUR (7) is fitter now for the new stable and has been thereabouts of late without threatening to win, but should also benefit from any tempo throughout. TASSIE DAZZLER (3) will most likely attempt to find the pegs first before possibly handing over to the more favoured stablemate BARBETTE (4), who is always around the mark in these races. MIDNITE DESIRE (5) draws an awkward gate but should get his chance to be running home in this sort of race. BLISSFULL RED (1) is a 14-start maiden with no real form to be excited about, but resumes here first up in the state without a trial, so the market may be the best guide. Selections:KIAVINO STRIDE (8), BARBETTE (4), KUHIO KREST (6), SWEET AMOUR (7) Staking Strategy:KIAVINO STRIDE should be too good if he somewhat brings his best form, with a little saver on KUHIO KREST. 4 unit win – KIAVINO STRIDE (8). 1 unit win – KUHIO KREST (6).

The other division of the No More Than Two Wins event for the older horses, where ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (2) looks to get his chance being first to the pegs. He has been good in both starts since arriving in the state from back-row draws and should take plenty of beating if he is able to hold the front. SPORT WATCHER (4) has some gate speed from an okay draw but would need to improve on her past two starts, where she has been disappointing after putting together some competitive performances prior. PHLOW JO (5) is a well-bred mare who has run some handy races and should be suited in a class such as this, with the possibility of being driven on speed. Similar applies to SPORTZSILK (6), who clearly has some ability when he puts it all together and has been going better than his figure form suggests. UNOBETTER (1) broke through for a deserved victory last start and should get his chance again from the good draw, while STANTON BREAK (3) is always competitive in these types of fields. OUR DANCE MONKEY (7) over-raced first up in the state and was beaten a long way, but her previous form and an okay trial since suggest she could be in the finish if she brings better manners here. Selections:ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (2), PHLOW JO (5), OUR DANCE MONKEY (7), SPORTZSILK (6) Staking Strategy:ULTIMATE GLADIATOR should be first to the pegs and be hard to run down. 2 unit win – ULTIMATE GLADIATOR (2).

MY BEAUTIFUL LIFE (3) was well backed first up back in the state and failed to finish off after making a sharp move down the back straight when last, albeit only beaten 10 metres. Expect she may use her good gate speed here to push forward from the draw and gets her chance to bring her best to the table. QUEENOFDANCE (8) and DEBT TILL WE PART (9) are always running home strongly and earning their connections cheques in these sorts of races, and this looks to be no different. Both would benefit from any speed on throughout and should be suited by the middle-distance journey. PUNTARNO STRIDE (7) somewhat drops back in grade here and has been thereabouts of late. He is another who would benefit from some genuine speed throughout from barrier seven. ALBY PRIDDY (1) and NOELS GIFT (2) weren't far away last start in similar fields and get their chance to finish on the podium from their nice inside front-row draws. Selections:MY BEAUTIFUL LIFE (3), QUEENOFDANCE (8), DEBT TILL WE PART (9), PUNTARNO STRIDE (7) Staking Strategy: Willing to give MY BEAUTIFUL LIFE another chance after disappointing first up when well backed. At her best, she should be winning here. 2 unit win – MY BEAUTIFUL LIFE (3).

The high-class race for the night brings together a competitive field, where I suspect DENVER MAN (3) will look to push forward from his draw and be driven aggressively in search of the front. Both of his runs since returning to the state have been very good, and if he holds that form, he will take plenty of beating here. Best to ignore TAPPY (5)’s last run after having to be restrained back in the field, with his form prior more than good enough to take this out if he can get a nice run in transit from the awkward draw. LADY IN LINE (4) has somewhat been hit and miss with her form, but expect she could be very dangerous late if saved up for one run, as she has shown in the past when winning. MY WAY (8) and DONNY IN PARIS (9) are the back-row horses and will be hoping for some genuine speed throughout to allow them to run home strongly back in this grade, while the others in the field would need to improve on their current form to win here. Selections:DENVER MAN (3), TAPPY (5), LADY IN LINE (4), MY WAY (8) Staking Strategy:DENVER MAN should sit on speed and take a lot of beating. 3 unit win – DENVER MAN (3).

A small field from the stand start rounds out the night, with the field made up from the Langley and Yole stables. SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (6) clearly has the best form of late but is the lone 20-metre backmarker here. He is normally a super-sharp beginner, however, so should make up that margin quickly and, with the small field, should be hard to hold out late. REPETITIVE (1) has been racing consistently in these sorts of races of late and will be looking to settle on speed and get his chance to break through for a deserved victory. OLLIES MEDAL (2) clearly has the most class in the field when he brings his best behaviour, so if he is able to get away safely, he looks one of the main chances if he puts his best foot forward. DONE WELL (5) has been okay at her past two starts since resuming and should get the chance to finish on the podium with any improvement. SHEEZA SOHO (3) and OUR BETTER BRO (4) wouldn't surprise if they bobbed up to win with the right run in transit. Selections:SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (6), OLLIES MEDAL (2), REPETITIVE (1), DONE WELL (5) Staking Strategy: Although he’s off the 20-metre handicap, SAPPHIRE GAMBLER should still take some holding out late with his usual sharp beginning. 2 unit win – SAPPHIRE GAMBLER (6). We kick the National Drivers Championship off with a very even race. It’s a very even night of racing overall. BAY LA VILLE (2) finished down the track here last start at Globe Derby when she was defeated by GRUMPYPANTS GRACIE last start. She has a better draw tonight and looks extremely dangerous with James Herbetson in the sulky. YOUVE BEEN SERVED (7) has the draw to overcome but her recent Victorian form looks good. She will be right in the mix tonight. NOT VICIOUS (10) and TWIN CONNECTION (3) are also chances.

JACKIE DANIELS (6) ran an encouraging first up race at Gawler last start when she was beaten by BALLADORO by 3.6 metres. She should be able to improve off that run tonight. ROCKAMARA (3) was a strong Melton winner last start. Her form is hard to gauge outside of that win so it may pay to watch her market moves. JAWSOFGOODTIME (2) and TAKE MY WALLET (7) are also chances.

LORD LOGAN (7) has had the six starts for three wins and has had an excellent start to his racing career. He is a major chance again tonight after his strong Victorian form over the last few months. DAISY BOUCHEA (6), SAMMY BARBARO (2) and FEEL THE MOMENT (3) are also chances.

CLARENDEN TRIBUTE (3) is well drawn tonight and has been racing well recently. His last start was a little disappointing but his win the start prior was impressive. He looks like a major winning chance tonight. LOCHINVAR LEADER (7), KETO (4) and WATCHMEDAZZLE (2) are all big chances in what is an extremely even race.

SEASIDE LADY (3) was a winner by 12.1 metres last start defeating PERFECT PLAYGIRL. She is a strong chance of leading tonight and she looks the one to beat again. MIKISPUR (6), REACH THE PEAK (10) and LINCS POOR BOY (2) are all big chances tonight.

SANTA CASA LANE (1) was a recent strong trial winner at Globe Derby and has first start for a few years tonight. He is a risk but that trial run was eye catching. The draw is a positive as well and is overall record is strong. He is worth strong consideration tonight. TUFFASNAILS (10) was impressive last start winning by 37.6 metres and running 1.54.8. Tonight is tougher but that win is hard to ignore. He is a major chance tonight. STAR OF WILLOUGHBY (8) should get a nice run through from inside of the second row. DELIGHTFUL DREAM (3) looks the next best.

SO SIRIUS (8) ran second behind an impressive REPELLING last start at Port Pirie. He should enjoy the second row draw and he has the potential to be a major improver tonight. PESCI (5) brings some strong Victorian form into this. It may pay to watch his market moves. ARTILLERY (7) and ZENARIO (3) are also chances.

HEEZ A VIBE (1) gets the inside draw tonight and finds a race that suits him. He could be a big improver with Angus in the sulky and against a race like this. HARRO HILL (3), IM ALL BUSINESS (6) and CHASE THE STARS (8) are also chances.

ALWAYSBEALADY (6) is racing a lot better than what her form suggests. She could be a major improver in this sort of race tonight. FE FE ON FIRE (2), VATICAN GREEN (3) and MISS OUT (1) are also chances.

REGAL ATTIRE (5) will love the mobile start and he has the speed to lead. He is a major chance tonight. THE VICARS GIRL (2) will enjoy the return to the mobile start tonight and she will enjoy being in a race where she can be on the pace. ALL THE TRIX (4) and MY BAD HABITS (1) are also chances. OVERVIEW: Plenty hinges on the start here in my opinion, and if HITTHEROADJACK (1) can burrow through and do enough to lead, then he has a great chance in the first on Cup night. He’s a one-paced horse who lacks push-button speed, but he was able to work to the top last Friday at Melton and they couldn’t get near him as he carved out good sections in the run home to score by a big margin at good odds. He will be hard to run down over 1609m if he gets things his own way. MISS ARI (9) is a very classy mare who just missed Group 1 glory last time out when a narrow second to star rival The Art Of Success in the Vicbred Super Series final and she looms as a key danger from the nice back row draw, MY UNCLE STAN (3) led, handed up and just missed ROYAL APPOINTMENT (8) last weekend but is flying and might be the horse that tries to cross HITTHEROADJACK (1), while CLYMENUS (4) had no chance in that same race from out the back but he’s knocking on the door and looks ready to win. Another to consider is BLAKE BOLAC (5), who dead-heated first-up at Geelong with MY UNCLE STAN (3). SELECTIONS: HITTHEROADJACK (1), MISS ARI (9), MY UNCLE STAN (3), CLYMENUS (4)

OVERVIEW: Very open trot here where you can make a case for most, but I’ll take a small chance on JACK SPRAT (3) for the fact I think he can work to the front. Last time at Melton, he led over 2240m and was only grabbed late by the in-form Sebastians Boy in what was a solid effort. The drop back to 1609m suits at a track he loves, with four of his seven career wins coming at this venue. KEAYANG LAVITA (8) has had excuses in recent runs, including Sunday when she made up huge ground from the 60m handicap to only be beaten 5.1m at Terang. If PROHIBITED GRACE (1) holds the front, she’d be the one to beat. I liked FREIGHT SHAKER (6) each-way last weekend and he ran well for fourth, but will benefit from the outing as trainer Chris Svanosio hinted that he was perhaps a little underdone there, while SKY FLAIR (10) ripped through the line late from a hopeless position in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series final for four-year-old trotting mares and she’s been going really well this campaign. The chances don’t stop there… SELECTIONS: JACK SPRAT (3), KEAYANG LAVITA (8), FREIGHT SHAKER (6), SKY FLAIR (10)

OVERVIEW: FERRIGNO (3) ran an absolute cracker for third from a mile back in a race six of these horses contested at Geelong on September 11 and then seemed to ruin his chances by racing too keen at Echuca last time. Happy to take a chance on him at likely a decent price as he looks ready to win. SCHWARZ (10) won a string of races in Tasmania by big margins before coming back across to the mainland for a heat of the Vicbred Super Series for four-year-olds, and he ran well to just miss the final. He draws wide on the back row, but has the Emma Stewart polish and looks to have plenty of scope. TELEMACHUS (8) ran well in a strong race for third at Terang on Sunday and should get a lovely trip behind fast-starter ASMILEANDAWINX (1), who had to work too hard last time but can improve drawn on the fence here. BACK: FERRIGNO (3) – 1 unit (each-way) SELECTIONS: FERRIGNO (3), SCHWARZ (10), TELEMACHUS (8), ASMILEANDAWINX (1)

OVERVIEW: DISTANT SUN (9) looks to strike a very suitable 0-55 grade event where he draws nicely on the back row. Last time at Shepparton, he came with a wide run in the last lap, and while well beaten by Centurion Dream, he held a big margin back to third. That horse won last Saturday night at Melton, so the form stacks up. He was actually only beaten in a photo for second and third by that same horse two runs prior when 2.5m behind the in-form Karbine, who has also won again since. Happily on top. MUSCLE VALLEY (7) was a good runner-up behind Itz Classic Gold two back and was competitive in a strong Need For Speed Prince heat last time out, CONSTANT (5) is always running home strongly in her races and is a major contender with the right trip, while stablemate DANCE FIGHTER (1) has been outclassed her past couple but did start a $2 favourite prior to that and can be a factor from the good draw. BACK: DISTANT SUN (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: DISTANT SUN (9), MUSCLE VALLEY (7), CONSTANT (5), DANCE FIGHTER (1)

OVERVIEW: ISOLATION (9) has been in red-hot form this campaign for Patrick Tomkinson with back-to-back wins at Geelong and Melton followed by a close-up fourth placing at HQ last weekend behind Royal Appointment. It was a good run considering the race was dominated by those on the fence and he didn’t get a lot of clear air in the straight. There looks some tempo on paper, and he should give this a real shake. Surprised if he’s not fighting out the finish. MAAS BETTING AGAIN (3) probably needs to lead to win but she’s fast off the arm and won three races from the front with slick last halves through June and July, OLLIES THE BOSS (1) led and beat KOSIMO (2) and CAPTAIN PINS (6) when scoring in a similar grade at Melton on August 29 and has been outclassed his past two, while TOPSIES BLING (7) has produced big finales to win easier races at long odds but is going well and will be closing off late. BACK: ISOLATION (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: ISOLATION (9), MAAS BETTING AGAIN (3), OLLIES THE BOSS (1), TOPSIES BLING (7)

OVERVIEW: Ripping edition of the Geelong Pacing Cup where MINOS (5) is fancied to score first-up from a break. He has had the two trials in preparation for this and heads here for his first outing since a fourth placing behind Captains Mistress and Leap To Fame in the Inter Dominion Pacing Championship Grand Final at Albion Park in July. He won a heat and placed second in another before that and looks a good chance of rolling across to the front for Lochie Cook, who is looking to add a second Geelong Cup to his mantlepiece after scoring with JILLIBY NITRO (4) in March this year. BULLETPROOF BOY (2) hasn’t raced since a slightly disappointing display at Melton on August 29 but is a star and gets a great chance if he’s able to find the fence, NEW SHUFFLE (1) ran two brilliant races through the recent Vicbred Super Series and draws to run well here, while SIR JIMMY (8) was only grabbed in the shadows of the post by Catch A Wave last time and should be a factor from inside the back row. BACK: NEW SHUFFLE (1) – 3 units (place) SELECTIONS: MINOS (5), BULLETPROOF BOY (2), NEW SHUFFLE (1), SIR JIMMY (8)

OVERVIEW: ROCKINWITHATTITUDE (7) is one of the country’s premier trotters and lines up for just the second stand start of her career as she looks towards a New Zealand campaign that will include a run in the time-honoured Dominion Trot there in early November. It’s hard to see how a 30m handicap will stop her here if she steps cleanly, which she has done in three recent trials leading up to her dominant first-up win at Melton on September 19. IMPERIAL MONARCH (6) ran well for second behind Hoppy last weekend at Melton and gets the 10m head start on ROCKINWITHATTITUDE (7), Ararat Cup winner MORE WANTED (4) is first-up here since July, and while he rarely wins, is a very honest type at this level, and JOHNS BOY (3) returns from a couple of Menangle runs but did beat ANTONOV (2) with a bigger handicap in his last Victorian outing at Maryborough. MEADOW VALLEY STAR (5) is first-up in the care of Tom Rundle and has place claims. SELECTIONS: ROCKINWITHATTITUDE (7), IMPERIAL MONARCH (6), MORE WANTED (4), JOHNS BOY (3)

OVERVIEW: A SPECIAL OCCASION (4) placed third in the prestigious Northern Derby in New Zealand before being shipped across to join the Michael Stanley stable here in Australia. He stepped out as a short-priced favourite at Ballarat on September 23 and absolutely bolted in, and I fancy he’s the class here in the last of the night. THE FINAL DANCE (1) draws to lead and is a talented type from the Emma Stewart barn who performed creditably through the heats, semis and final of the Vicbred Super Series for three-year-old colts and geldings, ANGELS WATCHING (8) made an early break but still got up to win impressively from three fence at Echuca last time and is a factor from behind the likely leader, while THE NAKED ART (7) has a horror gate but is a mare in form with two recent Melton Saturday night wins under her belt. BRINGSUSJOY (2), BETTORLEFTALONE (3) and FIRE MARSHALL (6) are perhaps others worth considering for the back end of trifectas and First 4s. BACK: A SPECIAL OCCASION (4) – 1 unit (win) SELECTIONS: A SPECIAL OCCASION (4), THE FINAL DANCE (1), ANGELS WATCHING (8), THE NAKED ART (7) 10-UNIT GAME PLAN R3 #3 FERRIGNO – 1 unit (each-way) R4 #9 DISTANT SUN – 2 units (win) R5 #9 ISOLATION – 2 units (win) R6 #1 NEW SHUFFLE – 3 units (place) R8 #4 A SPECIAL OCCASION (4) – 1 unit (win) EARLY QUADDIE 1,3,4,9/1,3,5,6,7,8,10/3,10/5,7,9 QUADDIE 1,3,9/1,2,5/7/1,4 Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW:FORTY LOVE (5) was heavily supported and ran a great race after working forward to find the lead in the early stages when a narrow second behind Fighter Command at Melton last week. He had no luck when sixth in the Super Series Final prior and he should prove very hard to beat under these conditions. OPERATIVE LINE (6) will also appreciate a drop back in class from his efforts at Metropolitan free for all level and should improve on his numerical form. He won the Stampede at Melton back in May. HOT DEAL (7) settled down last in a slowly run race and tried to sustain a long run out wide on the track when a game third behind My Ultimate Jimmy at Mildura on Wednesday. He is a versatile pacer and should run his usual honest race. RUFF NUT (2) and MADRIGAL (3) are both racing well enough to be worth thought in multiple combinations. BACK: FORTY LOVE (5) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: FORTY LOVE (5), OPERATIVE LINE (6), HOT DEAL (7), MADRIGAL (3)

OVERVIEW:TAURAS (6) was resuming since July when he was without cover early, got in behind the leader at the 1300m and tried hard for a distant second behind Gaelic Lady at Terang. He should benefit from that performance and he was going nicely at the trials prior so he is capable of going one better. COLLEAGUES (5) has been placed in both of his efforts since coming from Queensland. He gained a nice trail and was going to run a clear second before breaking stride at the 150m at his latest Charlton third and he will prove hard to beat if he delivers a fool proof display. VIXAN (4) competed in a couple of Super Series events against much stronger opposition prior to a sixth at Terang, where she made several errors. She is better than her form reads and is a possible improver. DRESSEDUPINTHECITY (1) was caught without cover early, restrained to be fifth on the markers and battled on fairly well for fourth last outing. She is a maiden from 51 starts but she could fill a place from the pole position. SELECTIONS: TAURAS (6), COLLEAGUES (5), VIXAN (4), DRESSEDUPINTHECITY (1)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG HUSTLER (7) backed up several smart trial performances with a big victory over Dispersion at Terang, where he pushed forward to find the lead and completely dominated his rivals in handy time. He is widely drawn but appears to have a promising future and should prove hard to beat again. BAD GRANDMA (2) is a debutante for trainer Andy Gath, which scored nicely at a Melton trial on Tuesday afternoon. She is related to three winners and showed enough ability at her latest trial to warrant consideration. LOUS MAMBO (4) is a juvenile gelding that hasn’t raced since a victory in a fast mile of 1.56.5 at Charlton in May. He hasn’t been to the trials but will give a forward showing if he is somewhere near his peak form. BRIDWOOD MAISEY (9) was safely held at a recent Melton trial performance but she did make it through to the Breeders Crown Final last season so she cannot be left out of calculations. SELECTIONS: KEAYANG HUSTLER (7), BAD GRANDMA (2), LOUS MAMBO (4), BRIDWOOD MAISEY (9)

OVERVIEW: SKADI (3) began quickly to find the lead and was able to score comfortably when resuming at Swan Hill. She is a good chance of finding the lead again here and she did well after parking on the outside of the leader throughout at her latest third so she is capable of returning to winning form. MISSMALACHITE (6) progressed forward from a similar wide draw to race without cover when a brave second behind Doctor Go Joh at Terang on Monday night. This race is no harder and she should give another bold showing. DANCIN WITH ELVIS (1) finished a close up fourth in the race won by Doctor Go Joh and should receive every chance from the pole position. He has had a few chances since his latest victory but he is not without a winning hope under these conditions. ESPERANZA (4) led out then took cover and used the sprint lane when a close second behind Major Lincoln at Stawell. He won at Kilmore three starts ago and is one of the leading chances again. BACK: SKADI (3) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: SKADI (3), MISSMALACHITE (6), DANCIN WITH ELVIS (1), ESPERANZA (4)

OVERVIEW:CONNIES PRESIDENT (8) galloped away from the standing start and lost his chance at Charlton last outing but he was a runaway winner over BETSY ANNE (1) prior and he is drawn to gain an economical trip. BETSY ANNE (1) led out then took cover when third behind Money Talks at Kilmore last outing. She is a fast beginner and performs best over the sprint distance so she has the conditions to suit. I AM SKYE CHIOLA (10) competed against stronger opposition in a Super Series event last outing and finished midfield. She is a tough type and scored at Ballarat on August 26 so she is worth an investment. LOVE WHO (4) finished quickly via the sprint lane when a game second behind Rastamon at Maryborough last outing. He is racing well and looms as one of the leading chances again. SELECTIONS: CONNIES PRESIDENT (8), BETSY ANNE (1), I AM SKYE CHIOLA (10), LOVE WHO (4)

OVERVIEW:YANKEE RAIN (6) was heavily supported and shot to the lead shortly after the start when she led throughout at Terang last week. That was her best performance of the season and a repeat effort will see her go close to winning again. TORQUE IN HEAVEN (9) was very wide on the home turn and finished off fast for second behind YANKEE RAIN (6) at Terang. He won at his two attempts prior and is capable of turning the tables with normal luck in running. MONSIEUR FLAMEL (7) is a fast beginner and should be competitive from the wide draw. He commenced from the inside of the second line, was shuffled back on the markers and stormed home late when an unlucky second behind Foregone Conclusion at Kilmore last time out. MEGAWATTS (5) came from a rearward position when second behind Krissy in fast time at Shepparton last outing and is racing well enough to figure in the finish. SELECTIONS: YANKEE RAIN (6), TORQUE IN HEAVEN (9), MONSIEUR FLAMEL (7), MEGAWATTS (5)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY SNIPER (4) had little luck from poor barrier draws during the Super Series then followed with a big win at Terang, where he outstayed the handy performer Heavenly Gem. He is building up a handy strike rate and should prove hard to beat again. POSTERIZED (3) has been able to lead throughout in two recent victories and is drawn to lead again so he must be respected. He dashed home in a slick final half of 56.8 seconds when he held off Blazin By at his latest victory. GOLD IN PARIS (9) won three races in succession prior to a second behind King Kasey in fast time at Stawell, where she parked on the outside of the leader throughout. She is racing in career best form and is one of the leading chances again. CALF PEN (1) faces a steep rise in class but he has returned to his peak form and has leading reinsman James Herbertson aboard so he cannot be dismissed. BACK: JILLIBY SNIPER (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: JILLIBY SNIPER (4), POSTERIZED (3), GOLD IN PARIS (9), CALF PEN (1)

OVERVIEW: FROSTY DROP (4) attempted to lead throughout and was gunned down on the line when second behind Yankee Mojoh in a slick mile rate of 1.54.1 at Melton last outing. She is a good chance of finding the lead again and is capable of going one better. JILLIBY ZUCCHINI (11) was held up for a run at a vital stage and finished off strongly for an unlucky second at Terang when resuming since December 2024. She would have benefited from the experience and looms as one of the leading chances. MAJOR ROY (9) raced without cover throughout in fast time when a brave second behind Themidnightexpress last outing. He hasn’t had much luck in three starts since resuming and he should be competitive again. FOREGONE CONCLUSION (7) has won five of his past seven starts and was able to find the lead from a similar wide draw at his latest victory. This is a race of more depth but he is worth thought again. SELECTIONS: FROSTY DROP (4), JILLIBY ZUCCHINI (11), MAJOR ROY (9), FOREGONE CONCLUSION (7)

OVERVIEW: DISPERSION (1) was held up for a run at a vital stage and stormed home for an eye-catching third behind Baystyle at Melton when on debut then chased hard for second behind Keayang Hustler last outing. He is a promising maiden and is ideally drawn so he must be considered as a winning chance. LAMBRO LOUELLA (3) finished fast from midfield when a big second in the Ladyship Stakes at Globe Derby. She delivered a top run last outing and should be competitive again. MYDEEPESTDESIRE (7) raced on the outside of the leader throughout and went down fighting when a brave second behind Like A Gazelle on debut. She should have derived benefit from the experience and is worth thought again. EZEE FORTITUDE (8) is a first starter for trainer Andy Gath, which finished off in a slick final quarter of 28.1 seconds to win a trial at Melton recently so she cannot be left out of calculations. BACK: DISPERSION (1) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: DISPERSION (1), LAMBRO LOUELLA (3), MYDEEPESTDESIRE (7), EZEE FORTITUDE (8)

JILLIBY BLISS (6) put together an impressive win at Globe Derby when she held on to defeat EMILY MEGAN by a head at Globe Derby. She will find the draw tough today but she looks the one to beat based off recent form. MAGICAL MADGE (1) galloped at a vital stage last week but she could easily lead today and run a strong race if she trots smoothly. REHAB LAD (2) and PLATINUMS SON (3) are also chances.

MAIN BEACH (5) was impressive in a much tougher race last start. Today is easier but he will still need some luck from a tricky draw on a tight track. If he can run like he did last start and pace smoothly he will be hard to beat. JUST MILZY (2), ULTIMATE SAFARI (8) and CLARENDEN ARCADIA (7) are also chances.

PARISIAN BANDIT (3) ran second behind DONT TELL ALICE last start after being three wide for the last lap. He finds a very winnable race today and is well drawn. He could possibly lead and if he leads will hard to catch. WELL WELL (6), BRUZER (5) and DASHING COWBOY (2) are also chances.

LOCHINVAR HAWK (1) was run down after nearly leading all of the way at Globe Derby last start. He is a good chance of leading again today and being hard to catch after that better run last start. MURRA LANE (4), BROBENAH GIRL (2) and MACHFREDDY (3) are also chances.

IMA DESTROYER (1) was very impressive last start when she equalised the track record at Globe Derby and defeated TAKEN BY WINE by 20.4 metres. Today will be tougher but she has the inside draw and she loves the mobile start. QUARTARARO (10), MAORI TATTOO (3) and NOTHING I WANT (2) are also chances.

EDGAR BROMAC (1) has put together some promising runs in the early stage of his career. He broke his maiden last start at Mildura. He has gate speed and is a chance of leading all of the way today. LORD MYRMECIA (5), LIGHTNING BLING (6) and WHENIMREADY (9) are also chances.

SRIRACHA (1) finds an easier race this week compared to his last start at Globe Derby. He will love gate one and he should have the speed to lead. He is a strong chance if he is at his best today. AMIRA MARIE (4), A MAJOR STARR (2) and FENG SHUI STAR (8) are also chances.

PERFECT PLAYGIRL (1) has put together some encouraging runs since joining the Pullicino stable. She should be able to hold the lead from gate one which is a big advantage on this track. NORMY (5) looks like a big danger after a very impressive win last start at Globe Derby. CLARENDEN SAKURA (3) and FLYIN TOMMY (2) are also chances.
